headline.caveat: PIMCO's reported subscription of the ~$27B A+ rated note issuance for the Hyperion campus

realized_to_date.caveat: financing closed Oct 2025; funds draw as construction proceeds

nature_md: PIMCO was the anchor buyer — approximately $18B — of the ~$27B of notes issued to finance the Hyperion data-center campus owned by the Meta/Blue Owl JV. The notes were rated A+ by S&P and priced around a 6.58% yield, wide for the rating; Morgan Stanley arranged the deal, described as the largest private-credit/corporate-bond financing for a data center ever. Bondholders' credit ultimately rests on Meta's lease payments plus Meta's ~16-year residual-value guarantee rather than on Meta's general credit.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Held across PIMCO-managed funds and accounts as fixed-income investments (A+ rated, data-center-backed notes). PIMCO is a fiduciary manager — exposure sits with its fund investors.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Debt on the JV/SPV's balance sheet, serviced by Meta lease payments. None of it appears as debt on Meta, which holds only a 20% equity-method stake — the core of the off-balance-sheet critique.

observations.notes: Wide for an A+ rating — an early data point on how the market prices single-tenant AI-infrastructure credit.
